extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for geometry problem solving consisting of 3,002 multiple-choice geometry problems collected from two high-school textbooks, with dense annotations in formal language for both problem text and diagrams.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A new geometry problem benchmark was built by manually collecting problems from two online digital libraries/textbooks, with annotators gathering each problem's text, diagram, candidate choices, and correct answer, and labeling problem goals and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry problems sourced from two popular textbooks for grades 6-12 via the McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline digital libraries, including problem text, geometry diagrams, four candidate choices, and correct answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem and labeled each problem with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were well-trained and had undergraduate degrees.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is collected from two popular high-school textbooks and annotated by well-trained undergraduate annotators, which may bias it toward textbook-style, SAT-style school geometry problems and the perspectives of those sources and annotators.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes limitations of prior geometry datasets and indicates Geometry3K is still a specific benchmark of SAT-style high-school geometry problems. It also states that limited dataset scale makes some neural semantic parsing approaches infeasible.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is positioned as supporting research in geometry problem solving and educational reasoning, with geometry problem solving described as important for developing students' abstract thinking.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Education level/grade information is involved: problems are drawn from grades 6-12 textbooks, and human evaluators are screened by educational attainment (high school or higher) and include graduates majoring in science or engineering.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating geometry problem solving algorithms, and its formal language annotations are used to train and evaluate text and diagram parsers as well as symbolic/interpretable solvers.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the code and data are available and that the dataset and baselines are released, but it does not describe update schedules, maintainers, versioning, or deprecation policies.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Problem text and diagrams are automatically parsed into formal language using rule-based text parsing and neural object detection.
